newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Saudi power firm to sign $500 mln bank loan.
newsitem.headline: Saudi power firm to sign $500 mln bank loan.

text.p: A Saudi Arabian electricity firm said on Sunday it would sign a $500 million loan with five banks to partly finance a major power project in the kingdom's eastern province.
An official at the Saudi Consolidated Electric Company - East (SCECO-East) said the 10-year loan, to help finance the building of the Ghazlan II power plant, would be signed in Khobar on Monday.
He named the banks as Chase Manhattan, Bahrain-based Gulf International Bank, Al-Bank Al-Saudi Al-Fransi Saudi British Bank and National Commercial Bank of Saudi Arabia.
The loan would be repaid in ten years, with the first five years as a grace period, the official told Reuters.

It would be used to partly finance the building of the Ghazlan II power plant and associated projects. SCECO-East, one of four major power companies in Saudi Arabia, would finance the rest from its internal resources, officials said.
SCECO-East earlier this month signed four contracts worth 1.159 billion riyals ($309 million) to integrate the Ghazlan II plant into its main power system to keep pace with surging domestic demand.
Last year, SCECO-East awarded Mitsubishi Heavy Industries a 4.155 billion riyal contract to build the 2,400-megawatt plant, which consists of four units, each with a capacity of 600 megawatts.
Ghazlan II is part of an ambitious Saudi programme to raise the kingdom's power capacity to 60,000 megawatts over 25 years from the current 19,000 megawatts.
